analysis: Documentation-only units examined. inference.md head 5354-5641 is mostly unchanged Qwen27 TP text (the changed head ranges are 3635-3638 and 4037-4240, outside these units). It describes native context, media ingress, pair grants and the MTP assistant; no security behavior change is visible in these lines. prefix-cache.md (head 1043-1044, 1078-1084, 1267-1320) documents a new Gemma 4 tensor-parallel prompt-prefix cache. It reuses QwenStagePrefixCache (memory) and QwenStagePrefixDiskTier (encrypted SSD). Records are scoped by Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes within the request's tenant partition. planScope binds plan, policy, receipt, artifact and both builds. Records are kept only after bilateral retirement, and failed requests keep nothing. Boundaries are agreed by a sealed vote and confirmed by a sealed restore. SSD configuration, key, owner-only directories, TTL, write cap and free-space floor are shared with the other cluster families (QwenStagePrefixDiskConfiguration). Relative to T-041/SEC-035, this extends the existing at-rest and TTFT-oracle surface to Gemma TP traffic. The documentation does not claim weaker crypto or scoping. It does not say how cross-account isolation works in local-cluster mode beyond the 'tenant partition' reference. The vote reveals boundary presence between ranks, but both ranks are the same operator's cluster. The exposure is the same in kind as the existing Qwen/GLM TP prefix tiers. The CBv2PagedPrefixRestore reservedTokens change affects memory reservation, not isolation. No regression is supportable from documentation alone. Integration should verify that the Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix source actually folds the tenant partition (coordinator cacheSalt) into both tiers' keys and the HMAC names. It should also check whether the T-041 affected_files and description need updating to cover the cluster QwenStagePrefixDiskTier/Gemma TP tier.
